subject: Dedicated capacity recap: reserved GPUs, isolation needs, scaling plan

Subject: Dedicated capacity recap: reserved GPUs, isolation needs, scaling plan

Hi Alex / Sarah,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to hear more about Acme's production plan for clinical summarization. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the main points, our proposed starting config, and next steps so we stay aligned.

Key pain points you flagged:
- Latency spikes during peak clinical hours (affects real-time note generation)
- PHI / regulatory requirement: data must be isolated and auditable (no cross-tenant co-mingling)
- Need predictable throughput for 99.9% uptime during business hours

Goals on your side:
- Deploy a dedicated inference environment that provides consistent latency (<150ms median on 2k-token prompts)
- Ensure VPC-level isolation and KMS integration for keys
- Start with a conservative capacity that can scale automatically for bursts

Redwood recommended starting configuration (subject to final sizing call):
- Reserved capacity: 4 x A100 80GB (dedicated pool) as baseline for the primary region
- Autoscale/burst: +2 GPUs available for peak windows (burst policy)
- Isolation: Private deployment option with VPC peering or private link; control plane still managed by Redwood unless you opt for Private on-prem package
- SLA targets: dedicated capacity SLA: 99.95% monthly availability for reserved pools; we can discuss a higher SLA for an additional contract tier

Attached: capacity_estimate.xlsx (initial sizing & cost), mutual_action_plan.docx (proposed milestones). I also attached a short config doc (acme_dedicated_config_v1.pdf) with the items we discussed.

Immediate next steps:
1) Vivek (cc'd) to confirm network/VPC details and any firewall rules required.
2) Alex/Sarah to share a network diagram and preferred time for a short technical deep dive with your infra lead.
3) Redwood to provide a formal quote and a draft MSA/SLAs once we confirm sizing.

Proposed timing: technical deep dive early next week; canary rollout target 2026-03-10 if we align on sizing and contract.

If I missed anything, shout — happy to update.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Alex / Sarah — quick technical follow up from our infra side.

1) Data flow & PHI: With Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPUs + private networking) your inference requests can traverse a VPC peering/private link to a tenant-isolated serving plane. The control plane receives only metadata (no raw prompt content) unless you opt into Redwood-hosted logs; we support customer-managed KMS and ensure audit logs (request id, timestamp, model version) are exported to your logging endpoint for full traceability.

2) Sizing options and latency: The 4 x A100 80GB baseline is a conservative start for mixed batch/real-time workloads. If your prompt distribution skews longer (>>1k tokens) we should consider 6 x A100 or 8 x A10G as an alternative to keep median latency under 150ms. We ran a similar workload in a payer customer and saw median 120-140ms at 2k-token with 6x A100 + KV cache warm.

3) Autoscaling & scaling plan:
- Base pool (reserved): 4 GPUs
- Burst pool: +2 GPUs (auto-attach during peak windows)
- Policy: autoscale based on queue depth + p50 latency target; warm-up prefetch for large KV caches

4) SLA & ops: Dedicated pools come with a 99.95% availability SLA for reserved capacity. For 24/7 mission-critical SLAs we can explore 99.99% with a commercial commitment. Our on-call ops will provide runbook handoffs and an incident playbook; we can include a shared PagerDuty escalation if desired.

I've attached a short configuration summary (acme_dedicated_config_v1.pdf) and the capacity_estimate.xlsx with estimated monthly OPEX ranges.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa: Redwood to produce a formal quote & draft MSA with the 4xA100 + 2 burst config.
- Acme: confirm network diagram and preferred timing for technical deep dive (we can do 45m).
- Target canary rollout: 2026-03-10; production ramp post successful canary.

Happy to hop on a call with your infra lead tomorrow or Monday.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
